title: Backstep
snippet:
During the backstep, from frame 11 to 14, the player has hyperarmor, i.e. infinite poise. That means, no matter what hits the player, they will not stumble and stay on their feet. For example, the player can backstep through the boulders in Sen's Fortress without being knocked down. Keep in mind that you will still take damage, since the hyperarmor frames do not grant invincibility. The backwards ninja flip does not have hyperarmor frames.
When inputing an attack directly after the backstep, the player will perform a running attack. This can be very useful in combat, by dodging an enemy's attack with the backstep, then striking back with a running attack.

title: Backstep
snippet:
Backstep -  Dark Souls - mechanic - lead 
 lead : Backstepping is a gameplay mechanic in Dark Souls.

A backstep is performed by pressing the roll key without pressing in any direction. The player will then take a leap backwards instead of rolling.

Backstepping also grants invincibility frames, but fewer than rolling. While rolling gives 11 i-frames, backsteps only give 4. Equipping the Dark Wood Grain Ring replaces the backstep with a backwards ninja flip with 8 i-frames. This may now seem like backstepping is generally worse that rolling. However, backstepping has two situational advantages over rolling.

The special lightning bolt projectile is calculated like any attack using the weapon's Physical and Lightning AR and the attack specific Motion Values (100 Physical, 110 Lightning). snippet: An easy way to obtain the Dragonslayer Spear is to downgrade the Lightning Spear dropped by the Mimic in Sen's Fortress to a +10 Spear, and then upgrading it to the Dragonslayer Spear.  overview : Havel's Ring is one of the first rings accessible to the player assuming the Master Key was chosen as the starting gift. It is a useful ring, allowing many classes to upgrade from slow roll to mid roll or better and giving players a wider range of equipment options without sacrificing mobility. Later, the player may want to invest in Endurance to free up their ring slot, although certain players may require both the ring and high endurance if they seek out the heavier weapons and armor. title: Heavy Armor Sets (Dark Souls II)
snippet:
Heavy Armor Sets (Dark Souls II) -  Dark Souls II - armor - lead 
 lead : For categorization purposes on this wiki, Heavy Armor Sets are armor sets in *Dark Souls II* that have a total weight of 30 or more.

Heavy armor sets, such as Havel's Set, are good for tanking because of their high defense and poise. They allow for moderate to high damage to be taken without killing the player, however no armor set can make the player invincible, so caution is still your best defense.

Heavy sets, while they provide high defense also make moving and rolling much harder. The Royal Soldier's Ring, the First, Second and Third Dragon Ring all increase Maximum Equip Load, thus possibly allowing for faster rolling.

Again, strong armor does not make a player invincible. So focus and concentration can still trump having heavy armor.

title: Heavy Armor Sets (Dark Souls)
snippet:
Heavy Armor Sets (Dark Souls) -  Dark Souls - mechanic - lead 
 lead : For categorization purposes on this wiki, **heavy armor sets** are armor sets in *Dark Souls* that have a total weight of 40 or more.

Wearing heavy armor will slightly reduce the player's stamina regeneration, along with certain pieces of other armor sets. Each piece of heavy armor will reduce the stamina regeneration rate by 2 per second for all body armor pieces, and 1 per second for all other pieces. Furthermore, if the player has an equipment load that is higher than 50%, they will suffer a further 20% stamina regeneration penalty. Using Havel's Ring allows one to increase their equipment load, allowing them to wear Heavy Armor more easily.

title: Kingseeker Frampt
snippet:
After ringing the first of the Bells of Awakening, Frampt can be heard snoring when passing through the flooded area of Firelink Shrine of which he will eventually emerge. Strangely, this makes a collectible, invisible "humanity sprite" (one that increases your character's liquid humanity by 1 point) spawn nearby. It is possible to collect this sprite by falling from the nest above or one of the ledges above, but the fall may kill the character in the process (forcing the player to run back to his bloodstain from the last bonfire they rested at). It is also possible to collect this sprite by "passing through" Frampt's room. It seems to often be near the fallen pillar that lays diagonally on the ground (one end of the pillar pointing to the starting Lordran Bonfire of Firelink Shrine, and the other end of the pillar pointing to the graveyard leading to the Catacombs).
Frampt is one of the few characters whose mouth moves when talking.

 lead : **Rolling** is a gameplay element in *Dark Souls*.

title: Rolling
snippet:
Rolling -  Dark Souls - mechanic - general_information 
 general_information : Contrary to popular belief, all roll types have 11 iframes except for the roll type associated with Dark Wood Grain Ring (also called Ninja Flip) which has 13 iframes. The main differences between roll types is the overall length of the animation coupled with Recovery Frames and Instability Frames. Instability Frames are the most critical aspect of rolling, as these are points in the animation where the player character will take 1.4x additional damage when hit. Dark Wood Grain Ring roll type is the only roll with no Instability Frames.

title: Rolling
snippet:
Rolling -  Dark Souls - mechanic - fast_roll_light_roll 
 fast_roll_light_roll : Players have a Fast Roll if their equipment weight is 25% or less of their maximum equipment load. Within the fast rolling category, there are four categories: Fast rolls have far fewer instability frames than Mid and Fat rolls. Fast Roll is one of the most ideal types of roll if the player is opting to roll, second only to Ninja Flip. While at Fast Roll weight, player movement speed will be at its fastest possible while sprinting and walking.

title: Rolling
snippet:
Rolling -  Dark Souls - mechanic - medium_roll_mid_roll 
 medium_roll_mid_roll : Players have Mid Roll if their equipment weight is 26% to 50% of their maximum equipment load. Just like the fast roll, there are several different categories that affect speed of recovery after the roll: Medium rolls have 14 instability frames in their animation meaning there are more frames where the player takes 1.4x additional damage than they have iframes. This means that if the player is at Mid Roll weight, they should lean into Poise and Defense mechanics rather than rolling. The 1.4x additional damage taken during Instability Frames is enough to partially or fully negate the defenses that player armor provides. While at Mid Roll weight player speed during actions like sprinting and walking will be reduced slightly.

title: Rolling
snippet:
Rolling -  Dark Souls - mechanic - dark_wood_grain_ring_roll_ninja_flip 
 dark_wood_grain_ring_roll_ninja_flip : To utilize the effect of Dark Wood Grain Ring the player character must be at or less than 25% of their current equipment load. This roll type removes all Instability Frames in the animation and grants 2 additional iFrames to this roll type making the total iFrames 13. This is the most ideal roll type if the player is choosing to roll.

title: Rolling
snippet:
Rolling -  Dark Souls - mechanic - slow_roll_fat_roll 
 slow_roll_fat_roll : Players have a Fat Roll if their equipment weight is 51% to 100% of their equipment load. Fat rolls have vastly more instability frames in their animation than iframes. This means that if the player is at Fat Roll weight, they should lean into Poise and Defense mechanics rather than rolling. The 1.4x additional damage taken during Instability Frames is enough to partially or fully negate the defenses that player armor provides. While at Fat Roll weight, player movement speed will be greatly reduced while sprinting and walking. **It is best to never be within Fat Roll weight range.**

Should 100% equipment load be exceeded, the player cannot roll and staggers if attempting to do so. Over encumbered players will not be able to sprint, they can only walk in a style that as been affectionally dubbed as "poop walking" by the community.

title: Scythe of Want
snippet:
Scythe of Want -  Dark Souls II - weapon - characteristics 
 characteristics : The Scythe of Want is an interesting weapon, boasting a unique moveset, impressive attribute scaling and high base damage, but yet it can not be augmented or enchanted in any way possible and is quite hefty in size and weight.

Due to this, the Scythe of Nahr Alma can actually outperform this weapon significantly, not only by being able to be enchanted, but also by having virtually half the weight of this scythe.

However, the Scythe of Want has an unusually-high critical modifier, making it a formidable threat when used for backstabs, guard break/ripostes or parry/ripostes.

It should also be noted that its two-handed strong attack is a viciously quick and powerful attack, especially because it deals its most damage to players who get close to its wielders, which in essence turn this into the most versatile weapon within the Reaper class.

title: Sulyvahn's Beast
snippet:
Sulyvahn's Beast -  Dark Souls III - enemy - trivia 
 trivia : These beasts bear close resemblance to the Beast of Darkness from the *Berserk* franchise, having distorted eyes, the same shaped mouth, and almost identical body structures.
They are also similar to the Hounds of Tindalos, Lovecraftian beasts featured in [https://lovecraft.fandom.com/wiki/The_Hounds_of_Tindalos a short story] by Frank Belknap Long. These Hounds are said to hunt down ambitious time-travellers, and materialize out of mist, similar to Sulyvahn's Beasts as well as Vordt and the Dancer of the Boreal Valley. In addition, the Hounds of Tindalos are associated with a blue, ichorous substance; a visually comparable dark-blue "pus" also drips onto the floor as the Dancer is summoned into her arena.
In the *Dark Souls: The Willow King* comic, the Mastroth Demon bears a very strong resemblance to Sulyvahn's Beasts.

title: Sulyvahn's Beast
snippet:
Sulyvahn's Beasts are highly susceptible to Bleed, and as such, using a Carthus Rouge and/or weapons such as the Uchigatana or Carthus Curved Sword are recommended.

If one has the Slumbering Dragoncrest Ring and/or the Spook spell, plus the Hidden Body sorcery, the two Sulyvahn's Beasts in the Water Reserve can be dealt with by using the Poison Spores skill from the Storyteller's Staff from an applicable distance to slowly whittle their health down, one by one. Simply approach one while under the effects of Hidden Body and the ring/the Spook spell, and use the skill, then back away to the far wall before the spell(s) wear off.

title: Sulyvahn's Beast
snippet:
Sulyvahn's Beasts can be staggered. If their head is struck with enough damage, it will cause them to rear back and expose their chest for a critical attack. If this attack fails to kill them, it will knock them down onto their back, causing them to flail about for a period of time before being rendered helpless to be finished off. However, if a single attack does not kill them while they are in this state, they will get back up and resume the fight, though they can still be killed before their recovery animation completes.

During its lightning attack, it is advised to hug their chest or their sides. The attack is telegraphed and is rather easy to avoid as it affects a limited area and does not track the target, giving the player time to heal or attack without retaliation.

snippet:
Sulyvahn's Beast -  Dark Souls III - enemy - strategy 
 strategy : These beasts are very aggressive opponents and can easily kill the player if they are unable to escape their vicious assault. It is recommended to evade their attacks rather than block them, as they can deplete stamina very quickly and will often interrupt attempts to heal. Attacking them from the sides can prove effective as long as the player keeps away from their heads, as their bite has a long reach.

title: Sulyvahn's Beast
snippet:
The first beast will suddenly appear behind the player when they start crossing the bridge and will vanish if they retreat under the arch; however, it will not regain any health and it is possible to kill it from a distance with ranged weapons. It is possible that the beast on the bridge, if not slain, will fall down to the swamp area below and attack the player when they go through it.

The two in the Water Reserve should be lured away from each other, as fighting both at once is very risky. It is advisable to try and lure the one in the far right corner first as luring the one to the left may cause both to attack. Among the largest weapons available, ultra greatswords are very slow but inflict tremendous damage with each swing, and their great length allows them to strike targets from farther away. Players that guard against attacks will eventually have their guard broken once their stamina is depleted, resulting in them staggering back and being prone to a critical attack.

 lead : For categorization purposes on this wiki, **light armor sets** are armor sets in *Dark Souls* that have a total weight between 0 and 20. They usually have the lowest defense of all the armor sets and provide little to no poise. They allow for fast movement and roll speed, without the need for high endurance or equip load-boosting equipment.

Light armor sets that require standard titanite for upgrade require less resources to upgrade: they only require 4 of each titanite type per 3 level ups (×1, ×1, ×2), which is less than the 6 required for medium sets (×1, ×2, ×3). The Chain Set, Hollow Soldier Set, and the Hollow Warrior Set are an exception to this rule.

If they find they are taking too much damage, then they can make the choice to switch to a Heavy Armor Set, and if they feel like they are too slow, or they take too little damage for the defensive properties to be worth the weight, they may choose to choose a Light Armor Set.
